title: Convert a Toilet to Dual-Flush: Two-Button Actuator and Valve Upgrades

locations.name: Bathroom in owner's house (probable)
locations.basis: Transcript references 'this bathroom down here' and 'the original toilet to the house we moved in about 20 years ago,' implying a home bathroom likely inside the house being shown.

summary: This Old House demonstrates converting an existing 3.5-gallon-per-flush toilet to a dual-flush system using a low-cost conversion device. The host explains how most uses are liquid flushes and shows how a two-button actuator (one for liquids, one for solids) can reduce water usage without replacing the toilet. The process includes measuring current usage with a temporary water meter, removing the old flapper and lever, installing a new dual-flush valve with a blue gasket, mounting the two-button actuator, and reconnecting the supply. When the bowl refill is insufficient after the initial install, they upgrade the fill valve to improve bowl refilling, enabling reliable liquid flush performance. The video concludes with a demonstration of flushing liquids and solids, noting significant water savings while maintaining effective solids flushing.

sections.title: Assessment, measurements, and plan
concepts: planning to convert to dual-flush without replacing toilet
sections.description: The hosts identify high water use from an existing 3.5 gpf toilet, show a temporary water meter reading (~330 gallons in 7 days), and discuss converting the existing toilet to a dual-flush system using a ~$25 conversion device rather than buying a new 1.6 gpf unit.

sections.title: Install new flush hardware and two-button actuator
concepts: removing old tank hardware (flapper, chain, and lever)
installing new flush valve with blue gasket
mounting overflow-tube bracket and securing with a cable tie
sections.description: After shutting off water, the old flapper is disconnected, the chain removed, and the tank lever is removed (noting left-handed thread). A new flush valve with a blue gasket is installed, and the overflow tube bracket is attached to hold the gasket in place. The dual-function actuator (two buttons) is assembled, oriented for liquids on top and solids on bottom, and connected to the tank.

sections.title: Troubleshooting, refill optimization, and final test
concepts: refill-valve upgrade to improve bowl refill
adjustable fill valve to increase bowl refill after smaller liquid flush
testing the liquid flush and confirming proper operation
sections.description: The team identifies that with reduced tank discharge, the bowl may not fill enough for reliable liquid flush. They replace the fill valve with a model designed to allow more water to refill the bowl while the tank fills, and they adjust the refill to deliver adequate bowl water. After installation, they test flushing liquids and solids, confirm the liquid button uses less water while solids still use the original volume, and verify the overall system saves water while maintaining performance.
